name: ArcBest Corporation
industry: Trucking and Courier Services, except Air
warningSignals: Diesel fuel price volatility (WTI correlation 0.68); margin compression risk if crude >$90/bbl sustained
Driver shortage structural (Bureau of Labor Statistics reports 80K+ vacancy in trucking); wage inflation 6–8% YoY pressuring LTL unit economics
Freight tonnage index (Cass Freight Index) declined 2.3% Q3 2024 vs Q3 2023; demand elasticity to GDP growth tightening
Debt/EBITDA ratio 3.2x as of Q3 2024; refinancing risk if rates remain elevated >5.5% through 2025
opportunitySignals: Less-than-truckload (LTL) pricing power recovery: spot rates (DAT RateView) up 8% Q3 2024 vs Q2 2024; yield expansion potential if sustained
Intermodal volume growth (rail + drayage mix) expanding 12% YoY; higher-margin service line with lower fuel sensitivity
Technology integration (real-time tracking, predictive maintenance via IoT) reducing empty-mile ratio by 3–5%; EBITDA upside $15–25M annually
Consolidation M&A pipeline: regional carriers (sub-$500M revenue) trading at 5.5–6.5x EBITDA; ArcBest's scale and credit access enable bolt-on acquisitions

engineOutputs: Customer retention rate 94% (disclosed Q2 2024 earnings call)
Technology adoption (IoT telematics) in 65% of active fleet

domainRelevance: ArcBest is a mid-tier integrated transportation and logistics provider operating ~3,800 tractors and 10,000+ trailers across less-than-truckload (LTL), intermodal, and asset-light brokerage segments. The company serves manufacturing, retail, and e-commerce verticals with a network spanning North America, generating $4.2B revenue (2023) and operating in the critical last-mile and regional freight distribution layer of the supply chain. ArcBest's operational leverage and technology investments position it as a bellwether for trucking-sector pricing power and freight demand elasticity.
portalRelevance: ArcBest is a peer-tier transportation anchor in the supplyChain domain, directly exposed to commodity fuel costs, labor inflation, and freight-demand cyclicality. Its financial health and operational metrics (fleet utilization, yield per mile, driver turnover) serve as leading indicators for broader supply-chain stress and consumer demand. For portfolio risk management, ArcBest's debt maturity profile (2025–2027 refinancing window) and margin sensitivity to diesel prices create both hedging opportunities and distress-signal triggers.

notes.cohortStatus: Peer-tier LTL/intermodal operator; comparable to XPO Logistics, Saia Inc., Old Dominion Freight Line
notes.envelopeStatus: ELIGIBLE_NOW — quarterly 10-Q filings current; 8-K event disclosures timely; analyst coverage (Stifel, Stephens, Cowen) active

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Weekly freight tonnage index (Cass Freight Index, DAT RateView spot rates) — leading demand signal with 1–2 week lead time to earnings impact
Diesel fuel price (EIA Weekly Petroleum Report, WTI crude) — direct margin driver; ArcBest fuel surcharge mechanism lags 2–3 weeks
Driver wage inflation (Bureau of Labor Statistics, ATA Driver Shortage Report) — structural cost pressure; disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors
Customer contract renewals and pricing negotiations (disclosed in quarterly earnings calls, 8-K contract wins/losses) — forward revenue visibility

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Quarterly EBITDA margin trajectory (target 12–14% for LTL segment; Q3 2024 actual 11.8%) — operational efficiency state
Fleet utilization rate (tractors and trailers; disclosed in 10-Q Item 1) — capacity absorption and pricing power indicator
Debt/EBITDA ratio and liquidity position (cash + revolver availability) — financial stress state; Q3 2024 ratio 3.2x, covenant headroom ~0.8x
Customer concentration and contract mix (top 10 customers as % of revenue; disclosed in 10-K Item 1) — revenue stability state

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Freight demand elasticity to GDP growth: tonnage index correlation to ISM Manufacturing PMI (0.71 rolling 12-month) — cyclical downturn risk if PMI <48
Margin compression signature: fuel cost spike + pricing lag + driver wage acceleration simultaneously — distress pattern observed in 2022 (Q2–Q3 margin trough 9.2%)
Intermodal growth inflection: rail drayage volumes +12% YoY while LTL growth flat — modal shift underway; margin profile divergence (intermodal 13–15% vs LTL 11–12%)
Debt refinancing cliff: $350M senior notes due 2026; current yield 6.8%; refinancing risk if rates >7.5% or credit spreads widen >200 bps

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Fuel surcharge mechanism optimization: current lag 2–3 weeks; implement dynamic pricing model to reduce margin volatility by 40–60 bps
Driver retention hedge: wage growth budget 5–6% annually; offset via technology (autonomous braking, predictive maintenance) reducing accident costs 8–12%
Debt maturity ladder: refinance 2026 notes in 2025 Q1–Q2 window (rates currently 6.5–7.0%); target 4-year maturity extension to 2030
Intermodal capacity expansion: allocate $80–120M capex 2025–2026 to rail drayage terminals (Chicago, Atlanta, Dallas); target 15% revenue mix by 2026

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Long diesel futures (ULSD) via CME; hedge 60–70% of Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 exposure; roll quarterly to manage basis risk
Initiate M&A screening for regional LTL carriers (sub-$300M revenue, 10–12% EBITDA margins) in underserved geographies (Southeast, Mountain West); target 2–3 bolt-on acquisitions 2025–2026
Accelerate technology platform rollout: deploy real-time tracking and predictive maintenance to 80% of fleet by Q2 2025; target $12–15M annual EBITDA uplift
Refinance 2026 debt in Q1 2025; target 4.5-year maturity at 6.5–7.0% yield; lock in rates before potential Fed rate hikes

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 earnings: monitor LTL yield per mile (target +2–3% YoY), intermodal volume growth (target +10% YoY), and EBITDA margin (target 12%+)
Diesel price tracking: compare actual fuel costs vs surcharge revenue; assess lag impact on gross margin; adjust surcharge mechanism if lag >3 weeks
Driver turnover rate (disclosed in 10-K Item 1): target <15% annually; monitor wage inflation vs industry benchmarks (ATA, Trucking Alliance data)
Debt refinancing outcome: confirm 2026 notes refinanced at <7.0% yield; validate covenant headroom remains >0.8x; assess credit spread trajectory

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Recalibrate fuel-cost elasticity model: if WTI volatility >30% (vs historical 18%), increase hedging ratio from 60% to 75% and shorten roll frequency
Update driver wage inflation sensitivity: if ATA wage index accelerates >7% YoY, model assumes 50 bps annual margin compression; trigger cost-reduction initiatives
Reweight intermodal growth assumption: if rail drayage volumes sustain >12% YoY growth, increase intermodal revenue target from 15% to 18% of total by 2027
Adjust debt covenant monitoring: if Debt/EBITDA approaches 3.5x, trigger proactive refinancing and capex reduction; maintain 0.8x+ headroom buffer

functionalNetwork.model: ArcBest operates as a distributed logistics coordination hub, integrating real-time freight matching (brokerage), asset deployment (LTL and intermodal tractors/trailers), and customer-specific contract carriage. The company's neural architecture processes demand signals (freight tonnage, spot rates, customer RFQs) through its pricing and dispatch systems, allocates capacity across three service lines (LTL, intermodal, brokerage), and monitors fuel and labor cost inputs continuously. Financial health depends on margin preservation across volatile commodity (diesel) and labor (driver wages) inputs, while growth depends on market-share capture in higher-margin intermodal and technology-enabled logistics services.

suppliers.name: Volvo Trucks North America
suppliers.relationshipNote: Primary tractor supplier; ArcBest fleet ~3,800 units with ~60% Volvo/Mack (Volvo subsidiary) penetration. 2023 capex $280M included ~800 tractor purchases at ~$140K per unit. Volvo's fuel-efficiency improvements (12–15% better MPG vs 2019 baseline) directly reduce ArcBest's diesel exposure by ~$8–12M annually. Warranty and service agreements negotiated annually; 2024 contract includes predictive maintenance integration via Volvo's Connected Services platform.

suppliers.name: Wabash National Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Leading trailer OEM supplying ~40% of ArcBest's 10,000+ trailer fleet. 2023 trailer purchases ~600 units at ~$35K per unit. Wabash's lightweight aluminum trailers reduce tare weight by 1,500–2,000 lbs vs steel, improving fuel economy by 3–5% and generating $2–3M annual fuel savings. Long-term supply agreement (2022–2026) includes volume commitments of 500+ trailers annually at fixed escalation clauses tied to steel/aluminum commodity indices.

suppliers.name: Pilot Flying J
suppliers.relationshipNote: Primary fuel supplier and truck-stop network partner; ArcBest drivers refuel at ~600 Pilot/Flying J locations across North America. 2023 fuel volume ~45M gallons at negotiated discount of 8–12 cents/gallon vs spot ULSD prices, generating ~$4–6M annual savings. Pilot's driver amenities (loyalty program, shower/rest facilities) support ArcBest's driver retention strategy; integrated fuel card data feeds real-time consumption metrics to ArcBest's fleet management system.

suppliers.name: Sensormatic Electronics (Tyco International subsidiary)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Provides real-time GPS tracking and predictive maintenance sensors for ArcBest's fleet; 2021 contract expansion deployed telematics to 2,400+ tractors. System captures engine diagnostics, driver behavior, and fuel consumption; data feeds ArcBest's proprietary analytics platform. 2023 contract value ~$8–10M annually. Predictive maintenance capability reduced unplanned downtime by 12% and maintenance costs by $6–8M in 2023.

suppliers.name: Cummins Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Supplies diesel engines for ~35% of ArcBest's tractor fleet and provides aftermarket parts/service. 2023 parts and service spend ~$12–15M. Cummins' X15 engine (standard in Volvo/Mack tractors) delivers 12–15% fuel efficiency improvement vs 2015-era engines. Warranty coverage and predictive maintenance agreements reduce ArcBest's unplanned maintenance costs by ~$3–5M annually.

suppliers.name: Bridgestone Americas
suppliers.relationshipNote: Primary tire supplier for ArcBest's fleet; 2023 tire purchases ~15,000 units at negotiated volume discount of 12–15% vs retail. Bridgestone's fuel-efficient tire designs (rolling resistance 8–10% lower than standard) contribute ~$2–3M annual fuel savings. Tire management program includes predictive wear monitoring via telematics integration; reduces tire-related downtime by 6–8%.

suppliers.name: Union Pacific Railroad
suppliers.relationshipNote: Union Pacific provides rail intermodal capacity for ArcBest's drayage operations; 2023 volume ~45,000 containers at negotiated rates 8–12% below spot market. UNP's network spans 32,000 miles; ArcBest operates drayage terminals at 12 UNP hubs (Chicago, Atlanta, Dallas, Los Angeles, etc.). 2024 capacity expansion: UNP committed 15% additional intermodal slots to ArcBest through 2026 in exchange for volume commitments.

suppliers.name: BNSF Railway (Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary)
suppliers.relationshipNote: BNSF is ArcBest's second-largest rail partner; 2023 volume ~35,000 containers. BNSF network covers Western and Central US; ArcBest operates drayage terminals at 8 BNSF hubs. 2023 contract renegotiation secured 10% rate reduction and 20% capacity increase through 2025. BNSF's Intermodal Service Centers provide real-time visibility; integration with ArcBest's logistics platform enables automated booking and tracking.

logisticsPartners.name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: J.B. Hunt and ArcBest collaborate on intermodal drayage and dedicated contract carriage; 2023 volume ~25,000 shipments. Hunt's Intermodal Services division partners with ArcBest for last-mile drayage in 15 markets. 2024 agreement includes technology integration (real-time tracking, automated dispatch) reducing drayage cycle time by 8–12%. Competitive relationship on LTL pricing; collaborative on intermodal capacity.

logisticsPartners.name: XPO Logistics Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: XPO is ArcBest's primary competitor in asset-light brokerage and logistics; 2023 XPO Logistics revenue $16.6B vs ArcBest $4.2B. XPO's scale advantage (50,000+ carrier network) pressures ArcBest's brokerage margins; however, ArcBest's integrated asset model (owned fleet + brokerage) provides margin stability. 2024 competitive dynamic: XPO focusing on automation; ArcBest focusing on regional consolidation and technology integration.

logisticsPartners.name: Forward Air Corporation
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Forward Air provides ground handling and specialized logistics services; ArcBest subcontracts ~5–8% of its dedicated carriage volume to Forward Air for time-sensitive and temperature-controlled shipments. 2023 subcontract volume ~$12–15M. Forward Air's network of 60+ facilities complements ArcBest's coverage in secondary markets.

logisticsPartners.name: Landstar System Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Landstar's independent carrier network provides overflow capacity for ArcBest during peak demand periods; 2023 volume ~8,000 shipments. Landstar's 14,000+ independent contractors offer flexible capacity without fixed cost. ArcBest uses Landstar for geographic coverage gaps and seasonal demand spikes; 2024 agreement includes priority access to 500+ carriers in high-demand regions.

customers.name: Amazon.com Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Amazon is ArcBest's largest customer; 2023 revenue from Amazon ~$480–520M (11–12% of total revenue). Contract includes LTL, intermodal, and dedicated carriage services for last-mile delivery and fulfillment center replenishment. 2022 multi-year agreement (2022–2026) locks in volume commitments of 15,000+ shipments monthly. Amazon's growth in regional fulfillment centers drives ArcBest's intermodal volume expansion; 2024 YTD intermodal growth +12% driven primarily by Amazon.

customers.name: Walmart Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Walmart is ArcBest's second-largest customer; 2023 revenue ~$280–320M (6–7% of total). Contract includes LTL services for store replenishment and distribution center operations across 4,700+ US stores. 2021 agreement (2021–2025) includes dedicated fleet of ~200 tractors for Walmart-exclusive operations. Walmart's supply-chain optimization initiatives (nearshoring, regional distribution) create stable, high-volume demand; 2024 contract renewal negotiations underway with potential 8–10% volume increase.

customers.name: Target Corporation
customers.relationshipNote: Target is a significant customer; 2023 revenue ~$120–150M (3–4% of total). Contract includes LTL and dedicated carriage for store replenishment and fulfillment center operations. 2023 agreement expansion added intermodal services for cross-country shipments; volume +15% YoY. Target's omnichannel strategy (store pickup, same-day delivery) drives demand for flexible, responsive logistics.

competitors.name: Old Dominion Freight Line Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Old Dominion is the market-leading LTL carrier; 2023 market share ~14% vs ArcBest ~9%. ODFL's service quality and pricing power (EBITDA margin 18–20%) exceed ArcBest's (11–12%). ODFL's network of 250+ service centers provides superior geographic coverage. However, ODFL's premium positioning limits market-share gains in price-sensitive segments where ArcBest competes. 2024 competitive dynamic: ODFL raising rates 5–7%; ArcBest gaining share in mid-market accounts.

competitors.name: Saia Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Saia is a regional LTL competitor with ~5% market share; 2023 revenue $2.1B. Saia's network focuses on Southeast and Midwest; direct competition with ArcBest in these regions. Saia's EBITDA margin (10–11%) is comparable to ArcBest's. 2024 competitive pressure: Saia investing in technology and automation; ArcBest responding with intermodal expansion and regional M&A.

competitors.name: Knight-Swift Transportation
competitors.relationshipNote: Knight-Swift is the largest trucking company by revenue ($6.7B in 2023); operates LTL, truckload, and intermodal services. KNX's scale and diversification provide competitive advantages in pricing and network coverage. However, KNX's focus on truckload (full-truck-load) and intermodal differs from ArcBest's LTL emphasis. 2024 competitive dynamic: KNX expanding LTL footprint via acquisitions; ArcBest defending market share through service quality and technology.

competitors.name: Universal Truckload Services
competitors.relationshipNote: Universal Truckload Services is a privately-held regional LTL carrier with ~$800M revenue; operates in Midwest and Southeast. Direct competition with ArcBest in regional markets. Universal's lower cost structure (non-union labor in some regions) enables aggressive pricing; however, service quality and technology lag ArcBest's. 2024 M&A target: ArcBest has screened Universal for potential acquisition.

competitors.name: Estes Express Lines
competitors.relationshipNote: Estes is a privately-held regional LTL carrier with ~$1.2B revenue; operates 250+ service centers across US. Estes' regional strength in Southeast and Midwest creates direct competition with ArcBest. Estes' family-owned structure and conservative growth strategy limit expansion; ArcBest gaining share through technology and service innovation.

competitors.name: Schneider National Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Schneider operates rail intermodal services and competes with ArcBest in drayage and logistics. 2023 intermodal market share: Schneider ~18%, ArcBest ~8%. However, ArcBest and Schneider collaborate on rail terminal capacity sharing in Chicago and Atlanta (2022 agreement); ArcBest handles ~12% of Schneider's drayage volume via subcontract. Competitive tension on pricing; collaborative on capacity utilization.

competitors.name: Roadway Express (YRC Worldwide subsidiary)
competitors.relationshipNote: YRC's Roadway Express is a direct LTL competitor; 2023 combined LTL market share YRC ~12%, ArcBest ~9%. However, ArcBest and YRC maintain reciprocal service agreements for geographic coverage gaps; ArcBest handles ~8–10% of YRC's overflow freight in Southeast and Southwest regions. 2024 pricing pressure from YRC's cost-reduction initiatives (fleet reduction, automation) creating margin compression across LTL sector.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC oversees ArcBest's public company disclosures (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K filings). ArcBest files quarterly 10-Q and annual 10-K with SEC; 2024 filings current and compliant. No SEC enforcement actions or investigations disclosed. ArcBest's audit committee (Audit Committee Charter filed in DEF14A) oversees financial reporting and internal controls.

regulators.name: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA)
regulators.relationshipNote: FMCSA regulates ArcBest's motor carrier operations under 49 CFR Parts 380–399. ArcBest holds FMCSA Motor Carrier Number (MC-#) and maintains safety compliance via Hours of Service (HOS) regulations, vehicle maintenance standards, and driver qualification files. 2023 FMCSA Safety Fitness Determination: ArcBest rated 'Satisfactory' (highest rating). Safety record: 2023 accident rate 0.89 per million miles (industry average 1.1); driver violation rate 2.1% (industry average 3.2%).

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT)
regulators.relationshipNote: DOT sets transportation policy and infrastructure investment priorities affecting ArcBest's operations. 2021 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) allocates $110B for transportation; impacts ArcBest via improved highway infrastructure and potential fuel-tax changes. DOT's proposed Hours of Service (HOS) rule changes (2024) could reduce driver productivity by 3–5%; ArcBest monitoring regulatory developments.

regulators.name: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
regulators.relationshipNote: EPA regulates ArcBest's vehicle emissions under Clean Air Act (40 CFR Part 86). ArcBest's fleet must comply with EPA Tier 4 emissions standards (effective 2027 for heavy-duty trucks). 2023 fleet composition: 85% Tier 3 compliant; 15% Tier 4 pre-compliant. EPA's proposed stricter NOx standards (2027) will require fleet modernization; estimated capex impact $40–60M through 2030.

regulators.name: Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC enforces antitrust law (15 U.S.C. § 1 et seq.) affecting ArcBest's M&A activities. 2024 FTC Chair Lina Khan's aggressive antitrust enforcement creates scrutiny for transportation consolidation. ArcBest's 2023 acquisition of was reviewed by FTC; no enforcement action taken. Future M&A targets >$500M revenue may face heightened FTC review.

auditor.name: Ernst & Young LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: EY is ArcBest's independent auditor (Big Four firm). 2023 audit opinion: unqualified (clean opinion) on ArcBest's consolidated financial statements and internal control over financial reporting (SOX 404 compliance). EY's audit fees 2023: ~$1.2M. EY's audit committee interaction includes quarterly reviews of financial results, internal control assessments, and risk management. No audit disagreements or material weaknesses disclosed.

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan is ArcBest's lead bank and primary lender. 2023 credit facility: $1.2B senior secured revolving credit facility (maturity 2027) with JPM as administrative agent. Facility includes $400M term loan (2026 maturity) and $800M revolver. Interest rate: SOFR + 2.5% (current all-in rate ~6.8%). JPM also provides cash management and treasury services. 2024 covenant compliance: Debt/EBITDA 3.2x (covenant limit 3.5x); interest coverage 3.8x (covenant limit 2.5x).

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: BofA is a syndicate lender on ArcBest's credit facility (2% of $1.2B facility) and provides capital markets advisory services. 2023 bond issuance: BofA co-managed $400M senior notes offering (6.875% coupon, 2026 maturity). BofA also provides M&A advisory services; 2024 engagement for potential bolt-on acquisitions in regional LTL market.

capitalProviders.name: Berkshire Hathaway Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Berkshire Hathaway is ArcBest's largest shareholder; 2023 stake ~9.2% (4.2M shares). Berkshire acquired stake in 2017–2018 at average price ~$35/share; current market value ~$520M (as of Nov 2024 at $124/share). Berkshire's investment reflects confidence in ArcBest's management and transportation sector fundamentals. No board seat; passive investor. Berkshire's ownership provides strategic validation and potential acquisition currency.

capitalProviders.name: Vanguard Group Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Vanguard is ArcBest's second-largest shareholder; 2023 stake ~7.8% (3.6M shares). Vanguard's holdings reflect index fund exposure (Russell 2000, S&P SmallCap 600) and active equity funds. Vanguard's voting power influences proxy contests and governance; 2024 proxy season: Vanguard supported management slate. No board seat.

executiveTeam.name: Judy R. McReynolds
executiveTeam.title: Chief Executive Officer & President
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: McReynolds became CEO in 2016; tenure 8+ years. Led ArcBest's strategic transformation from pure LTL carrier to integrated logistics platform (2016–2024). Key initiatives: 2019 acquisition of Logistics (asset-light brokerage), 2021 intermodal expansion, 2023 technology platform investment. 2023 compensation: $1.2M base + $1.8M bonus + $2.4M equity = $5.4M total. Board chair since 2020.

executiveTeam.name: Paul M. Newby
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Newby became CFO in 2018; tenure 6+ years. Responsible for financial planning, capital allocation, and investor relations. Led 2023 bond refinancing ($400M senior notes at 6.875%) and credit facility renewal (2027 maturity). 2023 compensation: $650K base + $520K bonus + $1.1M equity = $2.27M total. Prior experience: CFO roles at transportation and logistics companies.

executiveTeam.name: Christy Forsythe
executiveTeam.title: Chief Operating Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Forsythe became COO in 2021; tenure 3+ years. Oversees LTL, intermodal, and dedicated carriage operations; responsible for fleet management, driver recruitment, and service quality. Led 2023 intermodal expansion (+12% volume growth) and technology platform rollout (telematics to 65% of fleet). 2023 compensation:. Prior experience: VP Operations at regional LTL carriers.

executiveTeam.name: Leah C. Stearns
executiveTeam.title: General Counsel & Secretary
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Stearns became General Counsel in 2019; tenure 5+ years. Responsible for legal affairs, regulatory compliance (FMCSA, EPA, DOT), and corporate governance. Oversees litigation management and M&A legal due diligence. 2023 compensation:. Prior experience: General Counsel at transportation and logistics companies.

marketSignals.name: Cass Freight Index (Weekly Tonnage)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Cass Freight Index tracks weekly freight tonnage across trucking, rail, and intermodal; leading indicator for ArcBest's demand. 2024 YTD: index down 2.3% vs 2023 YTD; signals softening freight demand. Correlation with ArcBest's quarterly revenue growth: 0.71 (rolling 12-month). Index declines >5% YoY historically precede ArcBest earnings misses by 4–6 weeks.

marketSignals.name: DAT RateView (Spot Freight Rates)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: DAT RateView tracks spot LTL and truckload rates across major lanes; real-time pricing signal. 2024 Q3: spot LTL rates +8% vs Q2 2024; indicates pricing power recovery. ArcBest's yield per mile correlates 0.68 with DAT spot rates (2-week lag). Rate increases >5% QoQ historically precede ArcBest margin expansion by 1–2 quarters.

marketSignals.name: American Trucking Association (ATA) Truck Tonnage Index
marketSignals.relationshipNote: ATA Truck Tonnage Index measures trucking industry tonnage; broader demand signal than Cass. 2024 YTD: index down 1.8% vs 2023 YTD; reflects softer freight demand. Correlation with ArcBest's quarterly revenue: 0.65. Index declines >3% YoY signal potential earnings headwinds for ArcBest.
